headline: Revenue surges on CHP Merger; loss widens year-over-year
summary_short: Sonida Senior Living reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $207.6 million, up 69.3% q/q and 122.0% y/y on the CHP Merger, with a per-share loss of $0.52 that narrowed 78.2% q/q but widened from a $0.16 loss a year earlier.
summary_long: Revenue surged on the CHP Merger, which added 54 senior-housing operating communities; resident revenue rose 129.7% y/y to $188.0 million for the quarter. G&A rose on higher stock-based compensation and labor costs; interest expense rose on $930 million of CHP-related debt financing; depreciation rose with the larger asset base. Other income fell as an $8.8 million one-time employee-retention-credit gain in Q2 2025 did not repeat. Q1 2026's EPS loss had included a one-time $19.1 million deemed dividend from the induced Series A Preferred conversion, explaining most of the q/q narrowing. No forward guidance was given.
confidence_notes: Q1 2026 EPS included a one-time $19.1 million deemed dividend on the induced conversion of Series A Preferred Stock, the primary driver of the large q/q improvement rather than a change in underlying operating performance. Adjusted EBITDA (non-GAAP) rose to $48.8 million from $14.1 million y/y, arguably a cleaner read on the operating trend than GAAP EPS given CHP Merger transaction costs.

drivers.explanation: Sequential narrowing mostly reflects the absence of Q1 2026's one-time $19.1M deemed dividend from the induced Series A Preferred conversion.
Year-over-year widening reflects CHP Merger-related interest expense, G&A, and depreciation increases outpacing revenue growth, plus a non-repeating $8.8M ERC gain in Q2 2025.
Growth driven by 54 additional SHOP communities from the CHP Merger plus higher occupancy and rent rates; resident revenue rose 129.7% y/y.
CHP Merger added 54 SHOP communities, nearly tripling revenue; Adjusted EBITDA rose to $48.8M from $14.1M as new-community contribution outweighed higher operating and transaction costs.
